title: Payment Failed but Customer Sees Money Debited

raw_content.initial_message: My payment failed but the money is already deducted.
raw_content.context: Customer sees debit after a failed payment attempt. Often this is a pending authorization that reverses automatically. Policy: reassure without dismissing, verify transaction details, avoid asking for full card numbers, explain expected timelines, and offer escalation if it doesn’t resolve in the SLA window.

learning_objectives: Explain pending authorizations clearly without sounding dismissive
Collect the minimal details needed for investigation
Set realistic expectations and next update time
correct_sop_steps: Acknowledge frustration and reassure customer you will help
Confirm what they see: amount, timestamp, bank name, and whether it shows as 'pending' or 'posted'
Explain that sometimes failed payments still create a temporary authorization hold that reverses automatically
Clarify expected reversal timeline and offer to track it with a reference if available
If it’s posted/settled, escalate to billing review and request relevant transaction reference (without sensitive card data)
Set next update time and confirm you’ll follow up
common_mistakes: Asking for full card number or OTP
Not offering escalation when customer is anxious
sticky_notes: KEY: Validate the anxiety first. Money leaving the account feels serious.
TRAP: Never request sensitive payment credentials.
HINT: Ask whether the charge is pending or posted—this changes next steps.

bonus_points: Explains the difference between pending vs posted in simple language
Offers a clear ‘what I will do next’ summary

customer_persona_hints.secret_acceptance_condition: Will calm down if you explain pending vs posted and give a clear timeline and follow-up plan
